results.insert:
The CRDT concept was formally defined in 2011 by Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero and Marek Zawirski, and was initially motivated by collaborative text editing and mobile computing. CRDTs come in two main flavors: state-based CRDTs, which merge entire replica states, and operation-based CRDTs, which exchange individual operations. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict-free_replicated_data_type))

In practice, CRDTs are used in online chat systems, online gambling, and the SoundCloud audio distribution platform, and CRDT data types are offered by the NoSQL distributed databases Redis, Riak and Cosmos DB. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict-free_replicated_data_type))

results.insert:
A tsvector value is a sorted list of distinct lexemes—words that have been normalized to merge different variants of the same word. Sorting and duplicate-elimination are performed automatically during input, and optionally, integer positions and weight labels (A, B, C, or D) can be attached to lexemes to support proximity ranking and to reflect document structure such as distinguishing title words from body words. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-textsearch.html))

The tsquery type represents a text query and is used together with the @@ operator to test whether a tsvector matches the query, returning a boolean result. The tsvector type itself does not perform any word normalization; it assumes the words it is given are already normalized appropriately for the application. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-textsearch.html), [thegnar.com](https://www.thegnar.com/blog/postgres-full-text-search))

In practice, building a tsvector from raw text involves breaking the document into words, removing common stop words such as 'the', 'for', and 'is', and normalizing remaining words so that different variants of the same word are merged into a single lexeme. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/wagenrace/sql-and-postgresql-for-advanced-full-text-search-3cle))
